theme: अधियज्ञ और देहांत की चेतना | Adhiyajña and the consciousness at departure
context: Arjuna's questions remain unanswered. Here he asks who and how Adhiyajna is in this body, and separately how self-controlled people can know Krishna at death. Krishna's answers follow.
contextHindi: अर्जुन के प्रश्नों का उत्तर अभी नहीं आया है। यहाँ वे पूछते हैं कि इस देह में अधियज्ञ कौन है और कैसे है। अलग प्रश्न है कि प्रयाण के समय संयमी लोग कृष्ण को कैसे जानें।
sanskritDevanagari:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन |
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ||८-२||
transliteration:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko.atra dehe.asminmadhusūdana .
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo.asi niyatātmabhiḥ ||8-2||

wordByWord.meaning: The Adhiyajña; Krishna says in 8.4, “I alone am the Adhiyajña here in this body.”
In this body; the embodied field of action, sensation, and mind.
Destroyer of Madhu; an epithet addressing Krishna.
At the time of departure, here the time of death.
To be known, recognized, or realized; not merely intellectually conceived but inwardly grasped.
By the self-controlled; those who have disciplined mind, senses, and attention through practice.

spokenHindi: अर्जुन का दूसरा सवाल है: ‘हे मधुसूदन, इस देह में अधियज्ञ कौन है और कैसे है? और प्रयाण के समय संयमी लोग तुम्हें कैसे जानें?’ यहाँ अर्जुन अपना प्रश्न पूछ रहे हैं; कृष्ण का उत्तर अगले श्लोक में शुरू होगा। अधियज्ञ की पहचान और वह इस देह में कैसे है, दोनों समझना पहले सवाल का हिस्सा हैं। दूसरा हिस्सा यह है कि जीवन के अंतिम समय में भगवान् को कैसे जाना जाए। अर्जुन इसे साफ़-साफ़ पूछते हैं। यह श्लोक किसी व्यक्ति की मनःस्थिति या उसकी कठिनाइयों पर फैसला नहीं सुनाता। यह भगवान् से मार्गदर्शन माँगता है। आगे गीता स्मरण और साधना की बात करेगी। इस प्रश्न को हम अपने जीवन में भी रख सकते हैं: साधारण दिनों में भगवान् को याद करने और उनसे जुड़ने के कौन-से छोटे तरीके हमारे लिए सहज हैं? उत्तर पाने के लिए अगले श्लोक की ओर बढ़ते हैं। यहाँ मधुसूदन कृष्ण का संबोधन है, जिसका शाब्दिक अर्थ मधु का संहार करने वाला है। इस नाम से कोई नई प्रतीकात्मक शिक्षा निकालना आवश्यक नहीं है। सवाल पूछते समय अर्जुन सम्मान भी रखते हैं और अपनी अनिश्चितता भी खुलकर बताते हैं।
clearEnglish: Arjuna asks who and how Adhiyajna is here within the body and how the self-controlled know Krishna at the time of death. The verse raises these questions; Krishna's answer follows in the next verse. Adhiyajna concerns the relation between embodied life and the Divine, while the second question asks about knowing the Lord at life's end. The verse does not explain every person's experience at death, nor does it say that difficulty remembering Krishna, confusion, illness, or distress is a spiritual failure. The phrase “self-controlled” describes those addressed in Arjuna's question; it is not a basis for judging people whose awareness is impaired. We can receive the verse as an invitation to ask how remembrance and devotion may be part of life, without making claims about anyone's final state. Arjuna's directness is also significant: a question about death can be voiced respectfully, without pretending that the answer is already known. Learning begins by naming uncertainty carefully.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Arjuna asks who and how Adhiyajna is here in this body, and separately how Krishna is to be known by the self-controlled at death.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The who-and-how inquiry can prompt careful attention to identity and relationship, while the separate question about knowing Krishna at death invites reflection without judging anyone's final awareness.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY — Sri Swami Sivananda
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The DLS commentary says Krishna used certain philosophical terms in the last two verses of the seventh discourse, and Arjuna asks the Lord about their meanings.

practicalApplication.label: Final attention
practicalApplication.text: Each day, notice where your mind settles when you are tired, afraid, or under pressure. Train it toward remembrance rather than reaction.

practicalApplication.label: Body as field
practicalApplication.text: Treat your body as a place of practice, not only as a site of consumption: breath, work, rest, and speech can all become acts of orientation.

reflectionQuestion: What kind of attention are you building now, and what will it likely feel like when the body is no longer steady?
reflectionQuestionHindi: आप अभी कौन-सी स्मृति का निर्माण कर रहे हैं, और जब शरीर स्थिर न रहे तो वह अंततः कैसी लगेगी?
